record.notes: The Act received Royal Assent on 19 June 2025. Section 138 was not in force at Royal Assent (s.142(1)); the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (Commencement No. 5) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/31), made on 15 January 2026, brought it into force on 6 February 2026. The offences in new sections 66E and 66F of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 are triable only summarily and have a reasonable-excuse defence whose operation the Secretary of State must review in a report to Parliament within two years; section 66H allows prosecution within 3 years of the offence and 6 months of the prosecutor having sufficient evidence. Courts, including service courts, can deprive the offender of the image and anything containing it. Most of the Act is a general data law and out of scope; only section 138 is recorded here.
record.scope_note: Not an AI-specific law: the offence covers any image that appears to be a photograph or film of a person but is not. Included as the UK's operative instrument against creating sexually explicit deepfakes; only section 138 of a general data law is recorded.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the legislation.gov.uk page of section 138 (latest revised version; heading, text, 'no known outstanding effects', commencement annotations I1 and I2) and the Commencement No. 5 Regulations, SI 2026/31 (stored as the secondary source; made 15 January 2026, regulation 2 and the explanatory note), snapshots of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged on 17 Oct; and, stored 17 Oct 2026, the Act's introductory text on legislation.gov.uk and the King's Printer PDF as enacted, both giving Royal Assent on 19 June 2025 and the enacting formula. Version 1's remark that the Online Safety Act 2023 already criminalised sharing such images is not in a stored file and was removed from the notes.

judgment.status_reasoning: Section 138 was not in force at Royal Assent (annotation I1, s.142(1)); SI 2026/31 reg. 2 brought it into force on 6 February 2026, which is before today (17 October 2026), and legislation.gov.uk records no outstanding effects on it. 'In force' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Not AI-specific (it covers any purported intimate image) but the operative UK offence for creating sexual deepfakes; in with a scope_note under AGENTS.md section 10.
